A.ul: 3,000 mcg a day of preformed vitamin A (retinol) from supplements and animal foods. There's no upper limit for beta-carotene from food.
A.tableNote: Beef liver is extremely high: 3 oz has about 6,582 mcg, more than 7 times the daily value. Enjoy it occasionally, not daily.
tips: Beta-carotene needs a little fat to be absorbed. A drizzle of oil or ghee on carrots and greens helps.
Cooking carrots and spinach lightly actually makes their beta-carotene easier to absorb.
risk: People with gut conditions that limit fat absorption
Such as cystic fibrosis, celiac disease or Crohn's disease.
Young children and pregnant women in low-income regions
A.lowNote: Vitamin A deficiency is rare in the US but still common in some low- and middle-income countries.
A.suppWhen: Most people get enough from food. Supplements are rarely needed unless a doctor finds a deficiency.
A.suppPick: If your multivitamin has vitamin A, check how much is retinol (retinyl acetate or palmitate) versus beta-carotene. Retinol is the part that counts toward the upper limit.
interactions: Orlistat (Alli, Xenical), a weight-loss drug, lowers vitamin A absorption
Retinoid medicines like acitretin (Soriatane) and bexarotene (Targretin) shouldn't be combined with vitamin A supplements
myths: Carrots give you night vision.
Vitamin A keeps normal night vision working. It won't give you super-vision. That story was WWII propaganda to hide radar.
More vitamin A means better skin and eyes.
Too much retinol from supplements can harm your liver and bones, and cause birth defects in pregnancy.
faq: Is beta-carotene safe?
Beta-carotene from food is safe. Your body only converts what it needs. High-dose beta-carotene supplements raised lung cancer risk in smokers in large studies, so smokers should avoid them.
Should I avoid vitamin A in pregnancy?
You need some vitamin A in pregnancy, but avoid high-dose retinol supplements and liver in large amounts. Ask your doctor whether your prenatal vitamin uses beta-carotene.

B1.ul: No upper limit has been set. No harm has been reported from high intakes.
tips: Thiamine leaks into cooking water. Use less water, or use the water in dal or soup.
Parboiled rice keeps more B1 than polished white rice.
risk: Alcohol reduces B1 absorption. This is the most common cause of deficiency.
They often eat less and absorb less.
They tend to lose more B1 in urine.
B1.lowNote: Severe deficiency (beriberi or Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome) is a medical emergency, mostly seen with heavy drinking.
B1.suppWhen: Usually only needed for heavy drinkers or after bariatric surgery, under a doctor's care.
B1.suppPick: Thiamine (thiamine HCl or mononitrate) is the standard form. Benfotiamine is a lab-made version sold in some supplements.
interactions: Furosemide (Lasix), a water pill, may lower B1 levels
Fluorouracil (5-FU), a cancer drug, can block B1 use
myths: B1 boosts energy if you feel tired.
B1 helps turn food into energy, but extra won't energize you unless you're actually low.
faq: Can vegetarians get enough B1?
Yes. Whole grains, beans, lentils, seeds and fortified cereals are all good sources.
Why is white rice 'enriched'?
Polishing rice removes the B1-rich outer layer. Enriched rice adds some back.

B2.ul: No upper limit has been set. Extra is flushed out in urine.
tips: Light breaks down riboflavin, so store milk in opaque containers.
Dairy is the main source for many people. If you skip dairy, look for fortified plant milks.
risk: Vegans and people who drink little milk
They may need a little more.
B2.lowNote: Deficiency is rare in countries where milk and fortified foods are common.
B2.suppWhen: Rarely needed. High-dose riboflavin is sometimes used for migraine prevention, but only with a doctor's guidance.
B2.suppPick: Riboflavin is the usual form. Bright yellow urine afterward is normal.
interactions: No clinically important medicine interactions are known
myths: Neon-yellow pee means the vitamins aren't working.
It's just extra riboflavin leaving your body. Totally normal.
faq: Can riboflavin help migraines?
Some studies suggest high-dose riboflavin may reduce migraines in some adults. Talk to your doctor before trying it.

B3.ul: 35 mg a day from supplements and fortified foods. This doesn't apply to niacin prescribed by a doctor.
tips: Your body also makes niacin from tryptophan in protein foods, so a diet with enough protein usually covers it.
risk: Low intake of B2, B6 or iron
Your body needs them to make niacin from tryptophan.
Such as Hartnup disease or carcinoid syndrome.
B3.lowNote: Severe deficiency (pellagra) causes a sun-sensitive rash, diarrhea and confusion. It's rare today.
B3.suppWhen: Not needed for most people. High-dose niacin is a prescription cholesterol treatment and should only be taken under a doctor's care.
B3.suppPick: Nicotinic acid can cause flushing. Nicotinamide (niacinamide) doesn't. 'Flush-free' inositol hexanicotinate is absorbed less well.
interactions: Isoniazid and pyrazinamide (tuberculosis drugs) can lower niacin
High-dose nicotinic acid can raise blood sugar, affecting diabetes medicines
myths: Niacin flush means it's detoxing you.
Flushing is just widened blood vessels. It isn't a detox.
faq: Is niacinamide in skin care the same as niacin?
It's a form of vitamin B3, but skin creams act on the skin. They don't count toward your daily needs.
Should I take niacin for cholesterol?
Only if your doctor prescribes it. High doses can cause liver problems and raise blood sugar.

B5.ul: No upper limit has been set.
tips: Almost every food has some B5. Whole, less-processed foods have the most.
risk: Deficiency is extremely rare and only seen with severe malnutrition or a rare genetic condition.
B5.lowNote: Low levels are so rare that symptoms are mostly known from experiments.
B5.suppWhen: Not needed. A varied diet covers it.
B5.suppPick: Calcium pantothenate is the usual supplement form.
interactions: No clinically important medicine interactions are known
myths: B5 supplements cure acne.
There isn't good evidence for this.
faq: Is panthenol in shampoo good for hair?
It helps hair feel softer and look shinier, but it doesn't change your body's B5 levels.

B6.ul: 100 mg a day. Nerve damage has been reported with long-term high doses, and some health agencies now warn about lower doses too.
tips: Chickpeas are one of the best plant sources. Chole or hummus count!
risk: Such as rheumatoid arthritis or celiac disease.
B6.lowNote: Low B6 often happens alongside low B12 or folate.
B6.suppWhen: Not needed for most people. Check how much B6 is in any 'energy', 'stress' or multivitamin product. It adds up across products.
B6.suppPick: Pyridoxine (pyridoxine HCl) is the most common form. More is NOT better.
interactions: Some seizure medicines (valproate, carbamazepine, phenytoin) can lower B6
Cycloserine (a tuberculosis drug) and theophylline (an asthma drug) can lower B6
myths: Water-soluble vitamins can't hurt you.
Long-term high-dose B6 can cause numbness and nerve damage.
faq: Does B6 help with morning sickness?
Doctors sometimes recommend B6 for nausea in pregnancy, but only take it on their advice.
How do I know if I'm taking too much B6?
Add up the B6 in every supplement you take. If you have tingling or numbness in your hands or feet, stop and see a doctor.

B7.ul: No upper limit has been set, but high doses can mess up lab test results.
B7.tableNote: Beef liver has about 31 mcg in 3 oz, roughly a whole day's worth.
tips: Cook your eggs. Raw egg whites contain a protein that blocks biotin.
risk: It's picked up by newborn screening.
B7.lowNote: Real deficiency is uncommon. Thinning hair has many other causes.
B7.suppWhen: Most people don't need it. There's little evidence that biotin supplements help hair or nails unless you're truly low.
B7.suppPick: If you take biotin, many hair, skin and nail products contain doses 100+ times your daily need.
interactions: ⚠️ High-dose biotin can cause false lab results, including heart (troponin) and thyroid tests. Tell your doctor before any blood test.
Some seizure medicines (carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone) can lower biotin
myths: Biotin makes hair grow faster.
It only helps if you're deficient, which is rare.
faq: Should I stop biotin before a blood test?
Tell your doctor you take it. They may ask you to pause it before certain tests.

needs: 400 mcg folic acid daily, plus food folate
B9.ul: 1,000 mcg a day of folic acid from supplements and fortified foods. There's no limit for natural folate in food.
tips: Folate is destroyed by long boiling. Steam greens, or eat some raw.
Dals and beans are folate powerhouses. A daily bowl helps a lot.
risk: Folic acid before pregnancy helps prevent serious birth defects of the brain and spine.
Such as celiac disease or inflammatory bowel disease.
People with an MTHFR gene variant
A common variant that can lower folate levels a little.
B9.lowNote: Low folate can cause a type of anemia (large red blood cells). It looks a lot like B12 deficiency, so both are usually tested together.
B9.suppWhen: Recommended for anyone who could become pregnant: 400 mcg of folic acid daily, starting at least a month before pregnancy. Most others can get enough from food.
B9.suppPick: Folic acid is well studied and well absorbed. L-methylfolate is an alternative. Ask your doctor which suits you.
interactions: Methotrexate (for arthritis or cancer): don't take folic acid unless your doctor advises
Seizure medicines (phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproate) can lower folate
Sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) reduces folate absorption
Large amounts of folic acid can hide a B12 deficiency
myths: You only need folate once you know you're pregnant.
The brain and spine form in the first weeks, often before you know. Start before.
faq: Folic acid or methylfolate?
Both raise folate levels. Folic acid is what most research on preventing birth defects used. Ask your doctor if you have an MTHFR variant.
Do men need folate?
Yes, everyone needs 400 mcg a day for healthy cells and blood.

needs: Get most from fortified foods or a supplement
B12.ul: No upper limit has been set. Your body absorbs only a small portion of large doses.
B12.tableNote: Clams and beef liver are the richest sources: 3 oz has many days' worth.
tips: Plants don't make B12. Spirulina, seaweed and fermented foods are NOT reliable sources.
Vegetarians: 2–3 servings of dairy a day helps, but many still need fortified foods or a supplement.
risk: B12 is naturally found only in animal foods.
Less stomach acid means less B12 absorbed from food.
People taking metformin or acid reducers long-term
The body can't absorb B12 normally.
Babies of vegan mothers who breastfeed
Low B12 in breast milk can harm a baby's development.
B12.lowNote: Low B12 can cause permanent nerve damage if untreated, sometimes before anemia shows up. A simple blood test can check.
B12.suppWhen: Strongly recommended for vegans. Worth discussing for vegetarians, adults over 50, and anyone on long-term metformin or acid reducers.
B12.suppPick: Cyanocobalamin is cheap, stable and well studied. Methylcobalamin also works. Shots are used when absorption is the problem.
interactions: Metformin (diabetes) lowers B12 over time
Acid reducers: PPIs like omeprazole and H2 blockers like famotidine
Chloramphenicol (an antibiotic)
myths: Vegetarians get enough B12 from dairy.
Some do, but many don't. Getting tested is the only way to know.
B12 shots give everyone more energy.
They only help if you're low.
faq: How do I know if I'm low on B12?
Ask your doctor for a blood test. Your doctor may also check methylmalonic acid (MMA) for a clearer picture.
Is too much B12 harmful?
No upper limit is set, and extra is mostly not absorbed. Unusually high blood levels without supplements are worth mentioning to your doctor.

C.ul: 2,000 mg a day. More can cause diarrhea and stomach upset.
tips: Heat and water destroy vitamin C. Eat some fruit and veg raw.
Squeeze lemon on dal or sabzi at the end of cooking, not during.
Vitamin C helps you absorb iron from plant foods. Pair them!
risk: Smokers and people around secondhand smoke
Smoking uses up vitamin C faster.
Including some older adults and people with food insecurity.
C.lowNote: Severe deficiency (scurvy) is rare but still happens with very restricted diets.
C.suppWhen: Most people can easily get enough from fruits and vegetables. A supplement may help smokers or people who eat very little produce.
C.suppPick: Ascorbic acid works fine. Buffered forms (sodium or calcium ascorbate) may be gentler on the stomach.
interactions: Some chemotherapy and radiation treatments: ask your oncologist before taking antioxidant supplements
Combination with niacin and simvastatin may blunt cholesterol benefits
myths: Vitamin C prevents colds.
For most people it doesn't prevent colds, but regular intake may make them slightly shorter.
Megadoses are harmless because extra is peed out.
Over 2,000 mg a day can cause diarrhea and raise kidney stone risk in some people.
faq: Is amla really high in vitamin C?
Yes, amla is one of the richest fruit sources. Fresh is best, since processing and heat reduce it.
Does orange juice count?
Yes. ¾ cup gives about a day's worth, but whole fruit also gives fiber.

D.ul: 4,000 IU (100 mcg) a day for adults. Doctors sometimes prescribe more for a short time to treat a deficiency.
D.top3: Fatty fish, UV mushrooms, fortified milk
table: Soy, almond or oat milk, fortified
D.tableNote: Few foods have much vitamin D. Most people rely on sunshine, fortified foods or a supplement.
tips: Your skin makes vitamin D from sunlight, but glass and sunscreen block it. Short, sensible sun exposure helps. Avoid sunburn.
Vitamin D is fat-soluble, so take supplements with a meal.
risk: Skin makes less and kidneys convert less.
Indoor jobs, covered clothing or northern winters.
More melanin means less vitamin D made from the same sun.
Breast milk is low in vitamin D.
Vitamin D gets trapped in fat tissue or absorbed less.
D.lowNote: Low vitamin D is common in many countries, even sunny ones like India. A blood test (25-hydroxyvitamin D) is the only way to know.
D.suppWhen: Worth discussing with your doctor if you're in any risk group. A blood test helps decide the right dose.
D.suppPick: D3 raises blood levels more than D2. Take it with food that has some fat.
interactions: Steroids like prednisone lower vitamin D
Orlistat (Alli, Xenical) lowers absorption
Statins may interact
Thiazide water pills plus vitamin D can raise calcium too high
myths: Living somewhere sunny means you have enough.
Many people in sunny places are low, due to indoor life, clothing, skin tone and pollution.
More vitamin D is always better.
Too much raises blood calcium and can harm kidneys and heart.
faq: D3 or D2?
Both work, but D3 raises and keeps blood levels higher. D2 is the vegan option, though vegan D3 from lichen also exists.
How much sun do I need?
It depends on skin tone, season, location and time of day. There's no single safe number, so many experts suggest food and supplements over extra sun.

E.ul: 1,000 mg a day from supplements (about 1,500 IU natural or 1,100 IU synthetic).
tips: A small handful of almonds or sunflower seeds a day covers about half your needs.
Most Americans eat less than the recommended amount, though true deficiency is rare.
risk: Gut conditions that limit fat absorption
Such as Crohn's disease or cystic fibrosis.
Vitamin E comes mostly from fats and oils.
E.lowNote: True deficiency is rare in healthy adults.
E.suppWhen: Not recommended routinely. Large trials didn't show benefits for heart disease or cancer prevention, and in one big trial, men taking 400 IU daily had a slightly higher prostate cancer risk.
E.suppPick: 'd-alpha-tocopherol' is natural. 'dl-alpha-tocopherol' is synthetic and about half as strong per mg.
interactions: Blood thinners (warfarin) and antiplatelet drugs: vitamin E can increase bleeding risk
Simvastatin with niacin: may blunt benefits
Chemotherapy and radiation: ask your oncologist first
myths: Vitamin E pills prevent heart disease.
Large studies found no benefit.
faq: Does vitamin E oil help scars?
Studies are mixed, and some people get skin irritation. It doesn't affect your body's vitamin E levels.

K.ul: No upper limit has been set. Vitamin K from food and supplements has low potential for harm.
tips: Vitamin K needs fat to be absorbed. Cooking greens with a little oil helps.
On warfarin? The key is consistency: similar amounts of greens each week.
risk: Newborns who didn't get the vitamin K shot
Babies are born with very little.
Such as celiac disease or cystic fibrosis.
K.lowNote: Deficiency in healthy adults is rare.
K.suppWhen: Not needed for most adults. Don't start or stop vitamin K if you take warfarin without talking to your doctor.
K.suppPick: K1 (phylloquinone) is the main food form. K2 (MK-7) is common in supplements.
interactions: ⚠️ Warfarin (Coumadin) and similar blood thinners: sudden changes in vitamin K change how the drug works
Some antibiotics may lower vitamin K made by gut bacteria
Cholesterol binders (cholestyramine, colestipol) and orlistat lower absorption
myths: People on blood thinners must avoid green vegetables.
No. Keep intake steady from week to week, and your doctor adjusts your dose.
faq: Does K2 help bones?
Research is promising but not conclusive. Food first. Ask your doctor before supplementing.
Is natto worth trying?
It's the richest K2 food by far. It's an acquired taste, though!
